decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at team preview against their steel-heavy core of aegislash, corviknight, gholdengo, kingambit, dragapult, and archaludon, I'm weighing incineroar, garchomp, gholdengo, kingambit, sinistcha, and archaludon as my picks. Earthquake actually hits most of their steels super effectively except corviknight, which is immune as a Flying-type. Incineroar brings great utility with Fake Out, Intimidate, and Flare Blitz for coverage, so I'll go with incineroar, garchomp, and gholdengo, leading with incineroar.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since Incineroar leads, Fake Out should work turn 1, but Dragapult's Ghost typing makes it immune to Normal-type moves, so Fake Out fails there. I'm now checking Flare Blitz's effectiveness against Dragapult instead.

Parting Shot could drop Dragapult's Attack and Special Attack while bringing in a teammate for free, which seems more useful since Dragapult is already weak to Ghost-type attacks. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball would hit Dragapult super effectively, but Dragapult's higher speed means it could strike first if it switches in aggressively.

Garchomp seems like a safer switch-in since Dragon-type moves hit it neutrally and it outspeeds Dragapult at 169 vs 142, letting it threaten with Outrage or Earthquake before Dragapult can respond.

Actually, Parting Shot looks like the better call here—it drops Dragapult's Atk/SpA further while bringing in Garchomp safely for free offensive pressure.
